cohort: The study included 30 singleton pregnant women, comprising 15 who experienced spontaneous preterm birth and 15 age- and BMI-matched healthy controls who delivered at term, all selected from a larger group of 12,800 pregnant women.
finding: Serum apolipoprotein A-II (apoA-II) and alpha-2-antiplasmin (a2-AP) were identified as significantly upregulated proteins and potential new markers for predicting preterm delivery when measured in the midtrimester.
cross-section timing: Serum samples were collected at 15-20 weeks of gestation.
